tips.comment: I really rate Rosallion and he ran a blinder at Royal Ascot but it is hard to look past the brilliant Field Of Gold. Since finishing an unlucky 2nd in the 2000 Guineas he has looked imperious since and should be difficult to beat.

I did think a chance could be taken on the Aussie runner Carl Spackler here. His jockey took a firm grip on him off a slow early pace at Ascot, and he just got done for a turn of foot late on. The time backs up the fact it was a slowly run affair, and, considering his keenness, he stuck to the task well enough, and off a likely strong pace round a bend here he could be seen to much better effect. I feel like he could be one of the first to get to the pacemakers, and if he’s filled up enough he could prove harder to peg back falling down the hill. He has the class to be involved in this from his runs in the US, and overall I just thought he was far too big a price even if giving 8 lbs to some sparkling 3-year-olds is a tough ask.

Lady Iman drops back in distance to five furlongs at which she started her career impressively. She lost her unbeaten record to Beautify last time over 6f in a Group 2 at the Curragh but can pick up a Group 3 prize here.

The 2yo colt has 2 wins from 4. He ran a big race two weeks ago in the £134K Super Sprint, a close 3rd of 19, maybe hitting the front too soon and giving plenty of weight away to the front two who both had decent OR ratings. He can take another step forward in this Group 3 and has every chance in this company off level weights. Strong jockey booking.

Just five career runs for the 3yo filly. Trip excuse last time out. She was only beaten a nk in her previous race, which was a Listed contest over this 10f C/D, and that form is looking strong now. Her mark of 89 for this handicap looks very attractive. Strong jockey booking.

Wonder Star is an unexposed filly with only three runs. She won a maiden at Ascot in good style and then was tried in a listed race only 8 days later at Newbury, where she was only 8th of 10 but received a bump over a furlong out and weakened. Her mark of 82 gives her a good chance in this field.

Previously trained by Sir Michael, 2nd last year I think. Ralph Beckett's runners are still in and out, down a few pounds. Certainly capable talent-wise. Remains to be seen if it can improve after some poor efforts at a track it clearly acts on.

I was all over Sing Us A Song for the King George Handicap at Ascot but he came out of the stalls very slowly and raced plum last for most of the way. He made up a lot of ground late on to eventually finish 9th not beaten that far. The price here is disappointing but I have got to give him one more chance as he previously looked very progressive.

Sudu was impressive when he was let go at Epsom last time, and there looked to be plenty more to come off the back of that effort. Barely given a tap, he extended to be a 7L winner in the last furlong and gets hit with a 13lb rise. He’s 2lbs well in on that rating hike though, and looked like he could be going places with that effort so is taken to follow up here. Varian isn’t having the best of times, but has won two of the last four runnings of this.

Novelista is still a maiden but has been beaten in photo finishes in his last two races over 14f. The drop in distance to 12f may not be ideal, but if the going goes softer, it will be to his advantage. He ran behind Sing Us A Song at Goodwood over 10f as a two-year-old when they were 1st and 3rd in a maiden off level weights. He now gets ten pounds with William Buick riding him for Charlie Johnson, who likes to get a few winners at Glorious Goodwood.

3/12 winning favs, 8/12 top 3 in betting. 10/12 carried 9st5 or less. 8/12 rated 89+. The main factor here is that there is literally no pace on, Cape Breton being the only one who likes to lead and has the chance to make the most of that lead here. Anything over 7f here doesn't have a strong bias either way regarding pace. Looked good last time out with 6L from 2nd Tremorgio who's since held his own in some class 3s. Well bred, could still be improving and worth a chance here.

Highly promising daughter of Night And Thunder & Sweety Dream ( Dam's sire Dream Ahead ) who was last seen at Newmarket 105 days ago where finishing 5th/7 however than run is best excused and she was forced a lot wider than ideal in a race that wasn't run to suit however Charlie Appleby's Godolphin trained inmate remains with all potential in tact and arrives here in top nick and in very good heart well prepared to tackle this HKJC World Pool Oak Tree Group 3 stakes race and a good analysis of this contest clearly shows Romantic Style will have his favoured pace level at his disposal given the horses enrolled to run here with the track here at Goodwood likely to play well into his strenghs worth noting this smart individual has a class 1 listed win to his name here on British soil a Group 3 win over in France and a Class 1 listed win over in Dubai and can put this race straight to bed before moving onto better things jockey William Buick takes the ride and can give Romantic Style a promising ride here at Goodwood expect to see this good looking chestnut thundering home

3-year-olds have won the last three runnings of the Oak Tree, and that's the age group I'm concentrating on. Andrew Balding's Formal was highly impressive at Epsom on Oaks day, but then proceeded to disappoint at York against the boys in the G3 Criterion. She was the only 3-year-old to contest that race, and I'm happy to put a line through that run.

Solid form from the 3yo filly this year and she can be a big player in this Group 3. She lost by a shd in a Group 2 during May - solid form. She ran well in a Group 3 last time out, staying on well from the rear. Her ratings for those two runs do stand out in this group of runners. A step up from 6f to 7f could suit her.

4/12 winning favorites, 4/12 top 3 in the betting. 0/12 won last time out. 10/12 rated 100+. 5/12 had won a group race. Not a big bet by any means, however, looks overpriced in a possibly weak race when Eve Johnson Houghton has been going so well. Key piece of form here is her run over 1m here in May when nose 2nd to Crimson Advocate who since won a Royal Ascot G2 and finished 3rd in the Falmouth G1 at Newmarket. Had been receiving nearly a stone when 2nd that day, however, it showed she handles the course well, which with the tight winds and undulations here is a big plus.

Unexposed 3yo, 2 wins from 6. Back on his game four weeks ago after a couple of below par return runs. He was a very close runner-up that day in a decent contest, the field strung out behind the front three, earning a high rating. Every chance of some more improvement. He now takes on older runners for the first time and receives a nice 7lb age allowance from 18 of the 19 rivals.

Another 3-year-old colt with an e/w chance is Beckett's runner, who finished down the field in the Britannia Stakes LTO. But this class 3 is far easier. The trainer has a decent w/p strike rate at the track, and the colt remains unbeaten in all his races at this level and below, as well as a 2 y/o win at this festival last year over C+D.

Great Acclaim is tried in a first-time hood. He had four wins last season, and his handicap mark went from 68 up to 92. Although not winning so far this year, he was only beaten a short head by Cracking Gold at Newmarket in his penultimate race off 88.

Winner of this race last year from a pound lower, he looks to have been given a break at the right time to arrive fresh for another crack. Placed on his other two runs at the track, and won't mind what the weather does.

Didn't pick up a leg on her 2025 debut, but has been absent since that April run. So perhaps there is an excuse for that well below par effort. She was generally progressive last year, including when winning over this course and distance for a yard, which does very well at this track and is in sparkling form with three winners from their last five runners.

Thenandnow and Amelia Earhart finished 2nd and 3rd at Leopardstown over seven furlongs earlier this month. But Amelia Earhart could improve past her rival and get the win here with Jack Cleary taking off five pounds.

The model I run suggests Thenandnow can win this one. Thenandnow lines up here with the highest RPR of the 8-runner field but is not penalized for it in the weights. The eight runners all carry the same initial amount. Thenandnow is drawn in favorable stall 3, where the inside draw is statistically favorable, especially over the 7-furlong distance, which is closest to the first bend. Moel has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This was driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.
Ran Green on debut last time and is bound to improve from that run. Has decent breeding and would have a decent chance here.
Black Caviar Gold filly, a £270,000 yearling by Havana Grey out of Perfect Outing, is trained by P. Twomey and ridden by C. D. Hayes, and she is expected to make a winning career debut.
First-time outers have won this race twice in the last three years, and Bear Right could go well here for a yard who can get them performing on debut.

Bred for speed and an early start to racing, Trusty Tycoon tackles a decent enough little maiden and attempts seven furlongs. Pivotal dam was tried over 1 mile. Small trainer does okay with sprinters. Yudish Geedharry claims 7 lbs allowance.
Collecting Coin was only beaten a neck when 2nd at the Curragh last time out and has since been gelded so could come back after a 67 day break with a win.
Made his debut in a big field 6f maiden at the Curragh when a close-up 4th. Didn’t have the clearest of passages during that race and can improve on that now. Well worth considering.
Yet to win from 6 starts but has placed 4 times, finishing 2nd on 3 occasions. That form gives an each-way chance in this.

Jack Cleary utilized a 5lbs claim to ride Mississippi River to win over 1 mile at Leopardstown in June. The horse (still a colt) has arguably been a bit unlucky in two starts since (beaten favorite each time). Receiving weight from older horses, different tactics may be used this time. Sole 3yo (by Lope De Vega) in the race against older horses. Aidan O'Brien trained. Strong contender.
Expecting a strong performance here from this gelding, who has been pitched in tougher races than this. Lenient handicap mark given the pattern performance too.

Won this in 2023 and 4th last year off a 2lb higher mark. Two good runs in hot handicaps this season should have them spot on for a repeat and top jockey/trainer combination makes current 7/1 very strong Ew value here.

Seems to be drifting in the market and i'm not too sure why, so that's a bit of a worry. Has been running well though imo in decent races and does like it on the softer side which it is at the moment.
Has won 2 valuable handicaps in his last 2 runs and is on a steep upward curve. Still has more to offer and looks an ideal type for Galway.

This bottom weight looks well handicapped to be with the first time booking of a decent Apprentice to knock another 3lb off. The horse is already a course winner off the same mark and he even followed that up with a decent 5th of 16 off a 7lb higher mark so he clearly likes it around here. The 2nd last time out also suggests he's primed to go in again soon and today could well be the day.

The model I run suggests an upset from Dunum. This result has been driven by Dunum having the highest RPR of this large 14 horse race. Dunum goes out carrying a lower amount of initial weight compared to the majority of the other runners and can be advantageous over the 1m distance. Drawn in stall 2, which is statistically advantageous over the 1 mile distance, and can run the inside rail (less distance) with less weight on board. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Bear Profit is very consistent with 5 wins and 12 other first 4 finishes in his 32 starts on the flat. He has been in excellent form recently, winning at Leopardstown in June before finishing 2nd at Curragh and 3rd back at Leopardstown 19 days ago. He was denied a clear run there, so although up another 1lb, the 7lbs claim of Nicola Burns looks significant. He looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Class horse of the race, dropping down from Listed and Group company. The trainer has had four winners in the last two weeks at a near twenty percent strike rate. The jockey has had five winners over that timescale. Seven-time turf winner can reward at a double-figure price.

Monasterboice is trained by Noel Meade, who loves to have a winner at the Galway Festival. Monasterboice has won three times on the flat and been placed six times from fifteen starts. Needs to get back to the form of last summer.

Listed winner at age two when with William Haggas, Alpha Capture has won once and placed twice (including at Galway) in six starts for Willie Mullins since joining the highly respected stable. Strong second at Leopardstown on reappearance this year. Slow start left him badly placed last time. Merits respect with little weight difference between all of them in this handicap.
Put up a very bold bid last time out at 12/1 in a 0-110. Finished ahead of half of the field there. Drops to a 0-85 and has a major change.

Apache Outlaw has been falling down the handicap since last year when he won three times at Dundalk and once on the turf at the Curragh. He is now on 78, six pounds lower than his last winning turf mark and twenty pounds lower than his current all-weather mark. Should be competitive at Galway over 7f.

Likes this track and was 3rd in this race last year, but returned later in the week to put things right and won that race. Is drawn well and had a satisfactory seasonal debut run two weeks ago and looks like this is the target race.

Improved on his reappearance effort when finishing a close 5th over 7f, racing from the same mark as today’s. Was given a lot to do then, but tried in a first-time tongue tie and cheekpieces combination. Can do a lot better.

Summer Snow is off a career-high mark, but two wins in her last three starts suggest she is still of interest here. She has 5 wins from 30 starts and this year has won at Leopardstown over 8 furlongs in May and at Down Royal over 7 furlongs last month. She is up 9 lbs for that win, but 7 furlongs is her ideal trip and looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

I am going to throw this one in as well as my ew tip as they both have similar traites. Has also won over c & d and just the one race this year, but it was in March and really would have liked to see a more recent run, but is drawn well with a 10lb claimer and if fit on easing ground, could run my ew and nap tip close.
On A Session has won six times and placed 11 times from 50 starts on the flat. Has never won at Galway but placed on multiple occasions. Each way chance.

The model I run suggests a big upset from Titanium. This result has been driven by Titanium having the highest RPR of the 15-runner field but not penalized for it in the weights. All horses go out carrying a very similar amount of weight over the shorter 7f distance. Titanium has a disadvantage in being drawn in stall 13 and will need to overcome this to go close. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The handicapper has stopped dropping nine-year-old Loingseoir, but at a mark of 68, he is on his winning mark from last September at Fairyhouse. He has been competitive this season, just finishing behind rival Si Senior at Ballinrobe when 3rd last month, and previously just beaten a nose at Limerick in April when ridden by today's jockey, Nicola Burns.

The McCourt stable has been in hot form of late, and Rampage comes into this race off the back of two strong runs, with a 1st place backing up a promising runner-up effort. Gets weight off plenty of rivals today and looks likely to continue good form.

I'm more than happy with the current 20/1 odds I'm offer for Don Browne's 8 year old Mare SPECKLED MEADOW who 'Should' strip fitter for her run at Leopardstown 54 days ago after returning from a 197 day sabbatical. This Daughter of FOOTSTEPSINTHESAND finished 2nd in this contest last year off the same mark & Jockey & has ran well here on her 4 attempts. The ground currently sits at Yielding but with a bit more rain due it shouldn't bother this charge. Jockey Wayne Hassett has a 43.48% place strike rate here the past 5 years and a very impressive 60% place strike rate when riding for this yard the past year. Trainer isn't no slouch either with a decent 42.86% place strike rate the past year. 5 places, good odds with a pipe opener in the tank. I'm in.
Yet to win from 6 starts but has finished 3rd on 2 occasions. Needs to bounce back after disappointing on handicap debut last time. Each way chance if finding some improvement.

Lady Arwen looks interesting on first seasonal start for trainer Conor O'Dwyer. Has won two races since joining this yard off marks of 68 and 72 (OR67 today). Apprentice Jack Cleary claims five pounds. Capable at best if ready to go on first run for 237 days.
Always runs well here and has tongue tie fitted for the first time today, which could be a big plus. Off a good mark in an open-looking race, can go close.

The model I run suggests Lexington Dash can win this one. Lexington Dash lines up with the highest RPR of this larger 18-horse field but has not been penalized for it in the weights. All horses step out carrying a smaller amount of weight around this shorter 1-mile distance. Doesn't have any form on offer but has a huge price to make up for that in case it can go close. The model has issued a very low stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
A long time off the track and superior speed figures - a combination which pays a good dividend over the long term. Obviously the win frequency is low but patience is a virtue in racing.

Disappointing when sent off as the favourite for this race last year, but she had only run at this meeting two days earlier, so perhaps it came too quickly for her. Has looked as good as ever this season on the flat for a new yard and is very well treated on that level of form if she can ever bring it to her hurdling efforts.

The model I run suggests Radar Ahead can win this one. Radar Ahead lines up here with the highest RPR of the larger 18-runner field but has an official ranking that's closer to the lower middle order. This subsequently leaves Radar Ahead well treated in the weights around his 2m round trip. Won when last out 17 days ago and second on the run before that, so comes here with plenty of form to work with. The model has issued a 'very low stake' indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Brilliant Light can win this one. Brilliant Light lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 20-runner field but has an official ranking that leaves him well treated in the weights. Carries only 3 lbs less than the bottom weight. Two third-place finishes in the last 3 races but needs to find more to win this one. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

It has been a while since he last ran over hurdles, but all three of his career wins have come over the smaller obstacles, including a perfect 2/2 at this track. Could do with the forecast showers being on the heavy side, but is on a workable mark on the pick of his form.

The model I run suggests Hipop De Loire can win this one. This result has been driven by Hipop De Loire having the highest RPR of this larger 19-runner field but is not overly penalized for it in the weights. Steps out carrying the same initial weight as nearly every other runner and trusted jockey Paul Townend picking up the reins for Willie Mullins. Second when last out in only race, will come on from that and looks to improve to get first here. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
